newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Anti-APEC groups launch motorcade protests.
newsitem.headline: Anti-APEC groups launch motorcade protests.

text.p: Thousands of leftist protesters riding in colourful Philippine jeepneys with streamers flying took to the streets on Sunday in protest over the APEC summit their country is hosting.

Police used frequent roadblocks to slow down the three separate protest convoys. Protest organisers plan to drive from Manila to Subic Bay, the venue for Monday's summit some 80 km (50 miles) to the north.
"This is just harassment. They are trying to lower our numbers," Renato Constantino of the "Slam APEC" group, organiser of one of the protests, told Reuters.
A heavily-armed police SWAT team blocked one of the protests. Dump trucks were used at one point to block the progress of another protest but the demonstrators pushed them out of the way.

Police said they had been told to use "maximum tolerance" in dealing with the protesters but were nonetheless determined to prevent them reaching the heavily guarded summit venue on a former U.S. naval base,.
"Our concern is the traffic, that it will move smoothly. We've been told to give them maximum tolerance," police Major Armando Amparo told reporters.

Security officials are determined to prevent any embarrassment to the government while it plays host to U.S. President Bill Clinton and other leaders here for the annual meeting of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum.

APEC's 18 members are Australia, Brunei, Canada, Chile, China, Hong Kong, Indonesia, Japan, Malaysia, Mexico, New Zealand, Papua New Guinea, Philippines, Singapore, South Korea, Taiwan, Thailand and the United States.
One of the biggest groups drove more than 260 gleaming jeepneys, minibuses derived from the design of a World War Two-type Jeep. Each was packed with more than 20 protesters.
